title: post-interview-stream-of-consciousness-henry-cho
content:
30m after loop — raw stream-of-consciousness. Goal: capture instincts before the panel synthesizes and before the formal scorecard, so we don't overfit to the group's framing. Candidate: Priyanka Rao — senior runtime engineer. Role: low-latency serving (KV cache, batching), ownership of cold-start and hybrid quantization rollouts.

First impression (tone + soft signals): confident, calm, good communication bandwidth. Talks through tradeoffs rather than black-boxing. Small humor in answers, pleasant to pair with.

Technical read: strong systems intuition. Good at memory/layout tradeoffs; described a past project where they reworked KV cache eviction to be eviction-window-aware (not pure LRU) based on sequence-length distributions — specific numbers (reduced tail latency p95 by ~18%) which is plausible and consistent with an implementer account (gave brief perf graphs explanation). Comfortable with kernel-level tuning but not a deep GPU-kernel hacker (didn't claim authorship of custom CUDA kernels). That could be okay for the role if we pair with infra folks or rotate responsibilities.

Pairing exercise notes: asked to sketch an autoscaling strategy for bursty LLM traffic. Suggested a hybrid approach: small warm pool + rapid warm-up nodes with progressive cache-priming via shadow traffic. I pushed on cache-priming correctness (staleness, privacy) — they acknowledged tradeoffs and proposed TTL + probabilistic priming. Quick pseudocode sketch on whiteboard that was readable. When asked about failure modes, they enumerated cold-start, cache-miss storms, and partial hardware degradation; proposed circuit-breakers + fallback to smaller quantized models.

Edge cases / red flags: one slip when we dug into cross-tenant KV cache isolation — they initially conflated namespace isolation with encryption-at-rest; later corrected but delay suggests less direct experience with multi-tenant isolation in Dedicated products. Also sparse answers on rollout automation (feature flags + canary metrics). They talked about manual rollouts historically; might be weaker in SRE-style automation.

Non-technical fit: collaborative, asks good clarifying Qs, shows curiosity about infra cost-accounting (asked about token-cost dashboards). Expressed preference for small-team autonomy and owning a feature end-to-end.

Hypotheses to validate in follow-ups / take-homes:
- Priyanka has hands-on experience shipping cache eviction heuristics and can produce measurable perf wins (ask for code snippets or a short writeup of the eviction change + test harness).
- Less experience with heavy automation for rollouts — probe for CI/CD, infra-as-code examples and previous on-call playbooks.
- Verify comfort with GPU ops: not a kernel dev but pragmatic operator. Ask for one example of tuning a model runtime on GPU (latency regressions and root cause).

Recommendation (quick): lean towards hire / strong hire if bias-corrected. Primary gaps are automations/rollouts and multi-tenant isolation nitty-gritty; both are trainable and complement org strengths. If we pass, pair them early with an SRE/infra mentor and a short onboarding project: (1) write a canary rollout playbook + automations for model variant fallback, (2) reproduce a small cache eviction perf regression and fix it with tests.

Interview follow-ups (todo):
- Ask candidate for short artifact: 1–2 page writeup of the KV eviction change they mentioned + perf graphs or test harness. (Due in 3–5 days.)
- Quick follow-up call with Marcus to probe multi-tenant isolation and rollout automation (15–20m).

Scoring heuristics I'm using privately (micros):
- System intuition: high (8/10)
- GPU/kernel depth: moderate (5/10)
- Automation / rollout maturity: moderate-low (4/10)
- Team fit / communication: high (8/10)
- Overall tilt: 7/10 (hire if paired properly)

Notes to self: avoid groupthink in panel synthesis. Flag the automation gap explicitly in debrief so we surface training plan as mitigating factor, not an afterthought. Save this doc for hiring manager + Marcus; paste key bullets into the structured scorecard (separate doc).

Random crumbs I want to remember: candidate mentioned previous company used a custom telemetry aggregator called "Pulse" (ask Marcus if familiar). Candidate is NYC-based and ok with hybrid. Salary expectation was broad (deferred to recruiter) but said they prefer role autonomy to title.

End stream.
